text:
Maya G: Quick sync — we need a clean, lightweight partner escalation playbook for Q3 (marketplace + HW + SI). current handoffs are messy and we lose time determining who owns the first ack.
Arjun K: +1. can we standardize a single shared channel pattern and a 3-step handoff? eg: #partner-<short>-sev for urgent comms, and a companion private warroom when needed.
Samir P: Suggest: 1) Shared channel created + PD incident page linked; 2) first ack by partner success (5–10m), 3) escalation to Redwood oncall if no ack or if production impact. keep it simple.
Evelyn R: Also capture roles in the channel topic: partner L1, partner L2, Redwood L1 (oncall), Redwood L2 (eng). topic example: "L1: @acme-support | L2: @acme-eng | RDW L1: @redwood-oncall"
Maya G: I can draft templates. two asks: a) channel naming + topic convention, b) a short warroom checklist.
Arjun K: For naming: #partner-<vendor>-sev (lowercase, hyphen), e.g. #partner-acme-sev. Private warrooms: use #war-<vendor>-<yyyy-mm-dd>-<sev#>.
Samir P: For automation — ops-bot should create warroom and post PD link when someone runs `/sev create partner acme` from the shared channel. ops-bot: can we wire that?
ops-bot: (bot) command acknowledged — prototype webhook exists at https://hooks.redwood.dev/partner-sev. will post bridge + PD link on /sev create.
Evelyn R: Warroom checklist (short):
- Post severity, impact, PD incident link
- Owner (partner vs RDW) + expected ack window (5m partner, 10m RDW)
- Primary comms channel (shared channel) + private warroom link
- Triage notes + immediate mitigation steps
- Rollback/feature-flag owner if relevant
- Postmortem owner assigned within 24h
Maya G: Nice. include a one-line template to paste into the shared channel so partners know what to expect. here’s a draft:
```
@channel SEV: severity=sev-1 impact=production 
Partner: Acme inc. 
PD: <link> 
RDW Owner: @redwood-oncall 
Requested ack: 10m
Warroom: <link>
```
Arjun K: We should also add an escalation matrix shortform for quick scanning:
- 0–10m: partner L1 acknowledge and triage.
- 10–30m: Redwood oncall joins, begins diagnostics.
- 30–90m: escalate to RDW eng L2 + partner engineering if root cause unclear.
- >90m: exec update cadence begins (30m cadence) and consider capacity/fallback routing.
Samir P: For SLAs — partner contracts often define initial ack. fallbacks when partner unreachable: automatic takeover by Redwood after 10m for sev-1, 20m for sev-2. document in channel topic and in partner runbook.
Evelyn R: Add guidance for sensitive customers: if customer data/regulatory concern, always escalate to security and legal immediately (privately), then create the warroom.
Maya G: I'll draft a short runbook doc and add the templates to the partner-runbooks repo. Will also add a tiny checklist file at the root called PARTNER_SEV_QUICK.md.
Arjun K: Who's owning the first rewrite for the runbook? Maya you can lead, Samir + Evelyn review, I’ll handle automation tickets.
Maya G: Sounds good. I’ll push a PR by EOD tomorrow.
Samir P: :thumbsup: I’ll stub the /sev create webhook ticket in JIRA now (PROJ-1245).
ops-bot: (bot) created jira PROJ-1245 linking to webhook prototype.
Evelyn R: One last thing — archive policy: keep the shared channel for 7 days after incident then move to #partner-archive with a one-line summary. helps partners search old incidents without noise.
Maya G: Great point. adding that to the doc. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
Arjun K: Moving to tasks: Maya (doc), Samir (webhook/jira), Evelyn (runbook reviews), me (automation PR). tagging this thread for followup next week.
